_coding_rules.inclusion: An abstract drawn by 05 is kept as artifact-free only if all three hold: (i) no release language and no URL, which 05 checks mechanically; (ii) it gives no coined name to anything it built; (iii) its stated principal contribution is a finding, not a resource or a performance-improving method. An unnamed instrument built to obtain the finding (an unnamed benchmark, an unnamed measure, an unnamed evaluation framework) does not disqualify it and is recorded in instrument_built.
_coding_rules.name_kinds: named_model = a released model or model family named as an object of study; evaluated_dataset = an existing dataset or lexical resource the paper runs on; prior_work = a named prior method, architecture or theoretical construct the paper tests or uses; standard_metric = a field-standard metric abbreviation (F1, ICC); field_acronym = an abbreviation for a task or subfield (LLM, SLU, M2MS); introduced_task = a task the paper introduces under a borrowed name; language = a natural language. names_capitalised is true only when at least one name is of kind named_model, evaluated_dataset, prior_work or introduced_task; field acronyms, standard metric abbreviations and language names do not count.
_coding_rules.coins_own_term: true when the abstract introduces a noun phrase as its own construct and reuses it as the object of the finding. Recorded whether or not the term is capitalised, because the coinages of interest (sycophancy, lost in conversation) are lowercase. Borrowed terms the paper merely defines for the reader are recorded with borrowed=true and are not counted as coinages.
_coding_rules.closing_move: knowledge_claim = the last sentence states what is now known about the object studied; call_to_community = it tells the field what to do (a call, a stated need, recommendations, guidelines); future_work = it names what should be studied next; contribution_restatement = it restates what the paper offers without stating a finding; resource_release = it points at a released artifact.
_coding_rules.numeral_role: SETUP = the numeral states the size or extent of what was tested (models, parameters, datasets, participants, items, or the denominator of a scale). OUTCOME = it states how something performed or how large an effect was. One row per quantitative numeral as counted by 03_measure.
